contentAngles.title: Why physician edit rate beats BLEU in clinical AI
contentAngles.hook: A PM I met at a mixer measures ambient scribe quality by physician edit rate — not BLEU, not leaderboard scores.
contentAngles.nonObviousInsight: Production eval metrics that reflect how clinicians actually work are more honest than benchmark chasing — but edit rate alone won't catch consent audit trail gaps that ex-FDA engineers keep flagging.
contentAngles.rationale: Concrete, conversational, grounded in Jordan conversation; bridges practical metrics + trust gap without naming Jordan in a way that feels like name-dropping.
contentAngles.predictedAudience: Health AI PMs and ML engineers evaluating clinical documentation products

contentDrafts.body:
Last night at an SF health-AI mixer on frontier eval frameworks, the room was full of smart takes on model benchmarks and leaderboard skepticism.

Here's what almost nobody said out loud:

We still don't know how to **evaluate the agentic workflow** — tool calls, handoffs, escalation — not just the model output.

One speaker (Dr. Maya Chen, MedAI) framed evals as "the product surface clinicians trust" — not a gate before launch. I keep turning that over.

If the model scores well but the workflow breaks consent logging or audit trails — a gap an ex-FDA engineer I met kept pointing to — did you pass eval?

For PMs in regulated industries, this isn't academic. It's the difference between a demo that wins a pitch and a product that survives a hospital workflow review.

What's the eval metric you trust beyond model accuracy?

#HealthAI #LLMEval #ProductManagement #AgenticAI
